purpose: Cross-layer audit that separates canonical accessory identities from acquisition routes across PQs, accessory shops, TP/STP shops, Shenron wishes, Online Raids, Crystal Raids, gifts, DLC, and special events.
rules: One inventory identity may have multiple acquisition routes.
A route record is not evidence of a new inventory identity by itself.
Historical shop schedules are dated evidence and do not establish current availability.
Clothing and accessory components remain separate unless independently documented as the same collectible.
Naming conflicts remain explicit instead of being silently normalized.
Unresolved records are backlog items, not missing-data licenses for invention.

wish_reconciliation.name: Power Pole
wish_reconciliation.finding: Current and historical references in the research layer conflict on the exact accessory naming/route. Keep as a route record until in-game inventory naming is independently captured.

wish_reconciliation.name: Goodie Radish
wish_reconciliation.finding: Current Fandom, Ludo (2026), and older GameFAQs/PowerPyx references consistently identify the rare-item wish reward as Goodie Radish/Radish. Treat the names as aliases of one candidate, not separate accessories.

wish_reconciliation.name: Saiyuki Hood
wish_reconciliation.finding: Wish/special and TP Medal Shop records are alternate routes for the existing canonical identity; do not duplicate the item.

wish_reconciliation.name: Turtle Hermit Set

source_notes: The current wish evidence identifies the rare-item reward as Goodie Radish; older sources use Radish accessory, so these are retained as aliases rather than separate identities.
The Guru-expanded wish list explicitly identifies Turtle Hermit Set as the reward for I want to dress up more.
Official Bandai documentation establishes that TP Medals remained earnable and usable in-game after the 2024 transition away from direct digital-store sales.
Historical shop records are retained as provenance, not as claims about the 2026-09-16 active rotation.
